articles.body: Hunting 'Ghost Positions': The F-160 Rule and Defensive Design in System State Reconciliation It was 1:15 AM, and the trading system was running its routine midnight checks. Suddenly, the logs lit up with a series of critical warnings. The position_monitor had detected active, highly leveraged positions on the exchange—specifically, a 75x leveraged 1000PEPEUSDT long and a 20x leveraged ETHUSDT long. There was just one massive problem: our internal system had absolutely no record of opening them. In the high-stakes world of algorithmic crypto trading, these are known as "Ghost Positions." If left unchecked, our AI trading engine would assume these were its own trades and attempt to apply automated Take Profit/Stop Loss (TP/SL) logic. The result?

articles.title: How to Move 4K Video from Your Phone to an External SSD Without a Laptop
articles.excerpt: Your phone is full of 4K video and there is no laptop in sight. Good news: you can move those clips straight to a portable SSD with a single USB-C cable. No laptop, no paid app — just the phone, the d…
articles.body: Your phone is full of 4K video and there is no laptop in sight. Good news: you can move those clips straight to a portable SSD with a single USB-C cable. No laptop, no paid app — just the phone, the drive, and a file manager. Why an SSD, not a flash drive? 4K video is big and needs sustained write speed. A 10-minute 4K30 HEVC clip is about 1.7 GB, 10 minutes of 4K60 is about 3.9 GB, and 10 minutes of ProRes 4K on an iPhone can be 11.7 GB. Cheap flash drives often slow to a crawl writing multi-gigabyte files, while a portable SSD holds hundreds of MB/s. I ran the numbers myself from published bitrates (iPhone HEVC 4K30 ~170 MB/min, 4K60 ~400 MB/min, ProRes 4K ~1.2 GB/min).
articles.author: Miftahul Rizki

articles.body: TraceScope is an MIT-licensed plugin for DeepSeek Harness with three capabilities: functional impact analysis, design diff analysis, and crash analysis. Version 0.3.6 adds Local crash capture , a crash source that doesn't wait for crash reporting. GitHub: https://github.com/rebornace/dsh-tracescope | npm: @rebornace/dsh-tracescope A source that doesn't wait for reporting Crash analysis already works against APM services such as Firebase Crashlytics: it lists issues, opens the details, parses the stack, and writes the AI conclusion back. Every one of those services only knows about crashes that were reported and aggregated. A crash that never got that far simply isn't in the list. 0.3.6 adds Local crash capture . Crashes and ANRs are pulled straight from a USB-connected device.

articles.title: Direct Forwarding vs a Local Relay: How to Plan WAF Attack Logs for Syslog
articles.excerpt: Searching for how to forward waf attack logs to a syslog server usually starts with a destination address and a port. The more useful first decision is where forwarding should happen: directly from th…
articles.body: Searching for how to forward waf attack logs to a syslog server usually starts with a destination address and a port. The more useful first decision is where forwarding should happen: directly from the event producer, or through a local relay that handles delivery to a central collector. For SafeLine, that comparison needs a clear evidence boundary. The supplied official documentation explains application protection and viewing attack details, but it does not document a syslog exporter, an attack-log file path, an export schema, or forwarding configuration. This guide therefore compares two logging architectures and provides a validation checklist. It does not claim that either architecture is a documented SafeLine integration.

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day.

articles.title: Andy Weir's 'Exoplanet' just landed on Audible, but what actually makes an exoplanet habitable?
articles.excerpt: How would the crew of the Wild Blue Yonder fare on a real exoplanet?
articles.body: Imagine you’ve crash-landed on an alien planet. Your ship is destroyed, your oxygen supply is dangerously low, and the landscape around you is completely unknown. Where would you begin looking for clues to your survival? Surprisingly, the best place to start could be the star overhead. This is the predicament that three crew members of the Wild Blue Yonder face in Audible’s new sci-fi thriller, "Exoplanet." This sci-fi thriller is written by acclaimed comic writer Benjamin Percy, executive produced by Andy Weir (Project Hail Mary, The Martian), and features an all-star voice cast including Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo . Stranded on an unfamiliar planet, they encounter volcanic wastelands, unknown skies, and environments that seem to defy reason.

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.excerpt: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers…
articles.body: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world’s most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia. Operating since September 2022, the Russia-based ransomware group Qilin is the currently the most industrious ransomware-as-a-service gang, according to a report (PDF) this month by the cybersecurity firm NCC Group (KrebsOnSecurity profiled the administrator of the second most active ransomware group — The Gentlemen — in June).

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: OpenAI is sunsetting ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice next month
articles.excerpt: OpenAI is going all in on GPT-Live.
articles.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR OpenAI has announced that it will retire ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice on December 11, 2026. The company is focusing on unifying the voice experience through GPT-Live. Live video and screen sharing will continue to use Advanced voice until GPT-Live has this capability. Earlier this year, OpenAI rolled out a new voice model called GPT-Live . The Gemini Live rival joined ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice as yet another way to have more natural conversations with the chatbot. As the saying goes, three is a crowd, and OpenAI is ready to do some streamlining. OpenAI has announced that a big change is coming for ChatGPT Voice. On December 11, 2026, the company will be retiring Advanced and Standard voice.
